identity.title: Influence of the presence of tubulin C-terminal tail on kinesin-1's microtubule binding rate.

content.abstract: The binding of the ATP-bound form of kinesin-1 to a microtubule composed of the full sequence of alphabeta-tubulin heterodimers (MTs) and one composed of heterodimers with the disordered C-terminal tails deleted (DeltaCTT-MT) was studied experimentally by single-molecule landing rate measurements and theoretically by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Theoretical models of MTs and DeltaCTT-MTs comprised a total of 260 alphabeta-tubulin heterodimers each. The initial structure of the kinesin dimer was modeled with AlphaFold. For each microtubule variant, 10 simulations were carried out with 5 kinesin molecules placed near the microtubule surface (a total of 50 kinesin molecules). Both experiments and simulations have demonstrated that the deletion of tubulin C-terminal tails results in the increase of kinesin landing rates. This difference is likely to be due to a greater disorder of the C-terminal tail at the binding surface for MT than for its truncated variant. During simulations a change of kinesin domain orientation from that in the initial kinesin model occurred, which enable simultaneous microtubule binding by both domains. However, nonspecific binding was largely observed, which indicates that the simulations captured its initial phase only.
